<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Make sure to read the Contributing Guide before submitting your PR: https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
2. If this PR closes another issue, add 'closes #<issue number>' somewhere in the PR summary. GitHub will automatically close that issue when this PR gets merged. Alternatively, adding 'refs #<issue number>' will not close the issue, but help provide the reviewer more context.-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
This PR provides context plumbing through pkg/action, to eventually replace
Timeout (time.Duration) arguments. Backwards compatability is maintained by providing an extension
of kube.Interface that adds in context argument based methods, instead of time.Duration.

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
I've left some comments in the code, for areas I'm unsure of how to handle. I'll comment specifically on the lines
so they appear for easier visability.

Additionally, this PR relates to [bug 120816](https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/12086) which describes kubernetes crud operations, still running after a timeout. Part of the problem, not fixed by this PR, is the pkg used to do crub operations against the kubernetes api-server [cli-runtime/pkg/helper](https://github.com/kubernetes/cli-runtime/blob/v0.27.2/pkg/resource/helper.go#L246) doesn't support passing in a context to it's http.Request, but uses a context.Background() in all API requests. One option is to copy the code used in cli-runtime/pkg/resources, but add in a ctx argument, that can use the ctx plumbed in via this PR.

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Closes  #11971

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

No public API was changed.

Earlier `failRelease` could be called twice (when `ctx` was cancelled and the background job had an error).
Now `failRelease` can be called at most once - synchronized with a channel (instead of a mutex lock).

Added comment with true behavior - running the job in the background after cancel is a bit surprising...

Done small refactoring. All fan-in logic is in a small function.
